notes: IEEE 1516.1-2025 public-API two-attribute scenario: Divestiture If Wanted returns an empty set with no pending acquirer, then returns and transfers only the first attribute when only that attribute has a pending regular acquisition. The second attribute remains owner-held, and a later acquisition of it requires a new If Wanted call. The selected native requirement page-151-l132-43 maps to §7.1.2.1 only for the If Wanted branch; other composite divestiture paths and process behavior are not claimed. The adapter supplies the provider, endpoint, two-attribute FOM and names, callback model, and logical-time implementation. Current-source installed-package C++ primary/contract passed 4/4 under evoked/immediate callbacks. Java parity compiles against the official API-only JAR but has no provider-runtime evidence. This is not a conformance claim.
